title: Long vowels: ا و ي held for two counts

bigIdea.text: Three letters stretch the vowel before them: alif after a fatha ('aa'), waw after a damma ('uu'), ya after a kasra ('ii'). Hold them for two counts, twice as long as a short vowel.

proper.text: The madd ('stretch') letters are ا و ي. They make a long vowel only after their matching short vowel: fatha + ا = 'aa' (بَا), damma + و = 'uu' (بُو), kasra + ي = 'ii' (بِي).
A madd letter carries no mark of its own (no vowel, no sukun). It simply lengthens the vowel before it.
This natural madd (madd tabee'i) lasts 2 counts. One count is the time of one short vowel; keep every count the same length, like a steady pulse.
Not every و or ي is a long vowel. With its own vowel (وَ, يَ) it is a consonant, 'w' or 'y'. With sukun after a fatha (ـَوْ, ـَيْ) it is a glide, 'aw' or 'ay' (called leen), not 'uu' or 'ii'.

In this mushaf a long 'aa' is sometimes written as a small alif above the letter (ـٰ) instead of a full ا; it is still 2 counts (next lesson). The app's tajweed colours give these small long vowels the 2-count colour; full-size madd letters are left uncoloured, but you still hold them 2 counts.

visual.caption: baa · buu · bii — two counts each

memoryHook.text: Matching pairs stretch: fatha-alif, damma-waw, kasra-ya, two counts.

extras.text: Persian/Urdu readers: after a light letter the Arabic alif is an open 'aa' (as in 'father'), not the rounded Persian 'â' (close to 'aw' in 'law'). ي after kasra is 'ii' and و after damma is 'uu', never 'e' or 'o'.
Many teachers keep counts even by folding one finger per count at a steady pace.

note.text: Kasra + a final ya (written here without dots): 'ii', 2 counts.
Fatha + ا in the middle of the word.
Damma + و in the middle of the word.
و with sukun after a fatha: the glide 'aw', not a long 'uu'.
Here the long 'aa' is a small alif above ع: still 2 counts.

drills.prompt: Say بَا بُو بِي, two even counts each (fold a finger per count).
Short, then long: بَ بَا · بُ بُو · بِ بِي

tip.text: بَ: one count. بَا: two counts. The alif doubles the length; the vowel quality stays the same.
بِ: a short 'i'. بِي: the same 'i' held for two counts.

remnote: Madd letters == ا و ي (alif, waw, ya)
Long vowels == Fatha + ا = aa, damma + و = uu, kasra + ي = ii
و or ي with sukun after a fatha == A glide (aw, ay), not a long vowel
